key_results: Commercial QWP converts rejected field into Hermite-Gaussian-like two-lobe mode; polarization extinction ratio enhanced >100× over 2-lobe overlap reduction; first-order plate nonuniformities amplified by confocal geometry
comments: The confocal geometry's sensitivity to plate inhomogeneity and the resulting beam-size scaling provide diagnostic tools for characterizing plate quality.

model_io.model: Confocal QWP detection with momentum- and real-space analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: QWP nonuniformities generate spin-orbit coupling observable as transverse-mode mixing in confocal geometry
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ideal plate by symmetry suppresses leading momentum-space contribution; real-space nonuniformities produce observed 2-lobe transformation and extinction enhancement

title: Classification of magnetism and altermagnetism in quasicrystals
task: Classify altermagnetism in quasicrystals via symmetry and PQMC simulations
key_results: Altermagnetism more common in quasicrystals than crystals; Néel state on D4-symmetric Thue-Morse QC exhibits altermagnetic protection via mirror/rotation symmetry (not PT); AFM reserved for crystal translational symmetry
comments: The finding that broken translational symmetry in QCs enables AM with non-PT protection suggests QCs as natural platforms for exploring unconventional magnetism.

model_io.model: Half-filled bipartite Hubbard model on Thue-Morse D4 QC via sign-problem-free PQMC

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lack of translational symmetry in QCs enables altermagnetic phases protected by point-group symmetry
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 1D IRRPs (non-identity, non-inversion-odd for even n) exhibit AM; classification scheme validated across multiple QC symmetries

title: Satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution model under time-evolving turbulence
task: Model satellite-to-ground QKD performance under time-evolving atmospheric turbulence
key_results: GEO-to-Lijiang link enables day-and-night QKD under favorable conditions with limited daytime link margin; time-resolved Lchannel(t) and DCbgn captured via phase-screen turbulence model
comments: The work advances beyond time-averaged turbulence models to capture realistic temporal fluctuations critical for link reliability.

model_io.model: End-to-end satellite-to-ground QKD simulator with phase-screen turbulence

hypotheses.hypothesis: Time-resolved turbulence model reveals temporal loss fluctuations missed by time-averaged approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; identified daytime link margin limitation and validated mitigation technique effectiveness

title: Security risks of VOA-induced luminescence in chip-based quantum key distribution
task: Identify security vulnerability from p-n junction VOA spontaneous luminescence in chip-based QKD
key_results: VOA emission centered at 1107 nm; wavelength-resolved side channel enables wavelength-splitting attacks without disturbing quantum states; quantitative analysis shows non-negligible information leakage even from weak emission
comments: First systematic study revealing a previously overlooked implementation-level vulnerability in integrated photonics for QKD, highlighting need for security-aware device design.

model_io.model: p-n junction VOA with security analysis framework

hypotheses.hypothesis: VOA luminescence creates wavelength-resolved side channel exploitable for eavesdropping
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; wavelength separation from C-band enables attack without state disturbance; weak emission causes non-negligible leakage

title: Effect of random corrosion pit dimensions on ultrasonic guided wave propagation characteristics in rock bolts
task: Characterize ultrasonic guided wave attenuation in rock bolts with random corrosion pitting
key_results: Peak-to-peak velocity reduction exhibits logarithmic relationship with pit area; individual pit area controls waveform distortion and energy scattering independently of total corrosion area
comments: The study reveals that defect discretization under fixed total corrosion is important for nondestructive testing, previously overlooked.

model_io.model: Finite element model of rock bolt with random pitting defects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Individual pit area influences guided wave propagation independently under fixed total corrosion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; logarithmic relationship for velocity reduction; dense small pits cause anomalously high scattered energy

title: Validation of a dynamic evaporation technique for generating isoflurane/air gas mixtures standards to calibrate anesthetic gas monitors
task: Validate dynamic evaporation method (EN 1839) for preparing isoflurane calibration gas standards
key_results: Correlation coefficient r² = 0.9998 over full clinical range (0–8 vol%); LOD = 0.08 vol%, LOQ = 0.27 vol%; concentrations 0.70–8 vol% comply with EN 1839 uncertainty; method suitable for routine anesthetic gas monitor calibration
comments: Repurposing a flammability-testing technique for clinical gas calibration demonstrates practical applicability with excellent metrological performance.

model_io.model: Dynamic evaporation and mixing (EN 1839 Method T) for isoflurane-air generation

hypotheses.hypothesis: EN 1839 dynamic evaporation method produces isoflurane calibration mixtures meeting metrological requirements
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; r² = 0.9998, LOD/LOQ acceptable; 0.70–8 vol% complies with EN 1839 uncertainty; validated for clinical use

title: SiO -formation and -condensation with hydrogen in carbon free conditions
task: Enhance SiO formation and condensation kinetics using hydrogen as carbon replacement
key_results: H₂ increases diffusion rate constant to 0.010 min⁻¹ vs. 0.006 min⁻¹ in Ar; produces finer, well-dispersed condensates with reduced wall fouling
comments: Hydrogen's higher diffusivity accelerates interfacial SiOₓ layer transport, offering practical advantages for CO₂-free silicon production.

model_io.model: 1-D diffusion-controlled (D1) kinetic model

hypotheses.hypothesis: H₂ enhances diffusion through interfacial SiOₓ layer compared to Ar
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; k increased by 67%; finer condensates with reduced fouling observed

title: DINO-prior guided detector for limited-label cross-process steel surface defect detection
task: Improve cross-process steel defect detection under limited labels via DINO-prior guided anomaly detection
key_results: mAP@0.5 improvements: +1.9 pp over D-FINE-X, +6.0 pp over Dome-DETR-L on NEU/GC10; cross-domain 10% label: +8.5 pp and +7.7 pp over D-FINE-X; 89.70M params, 12.70 ms latency (FP16)
comments: Leveraging self-supervised DINO embeddings as cross-process normality priors is elegant and effective, though adds substantial frozen encoder computation.

model_io.model: DINO-Prior Guided Detector (DPG-Det) with frozen DINOv2 encoder and multi-scale detector

hypotheses.hypothesis: DINOv2 normality priors transferred via anomaly-prior feature modulation improve cross-process defect detection with limited labels
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; substantial mAP gains over baselines in both single-domain and cross-domain settings

title: The effect of different liquids on paper strength demonstrates the central role of hydrogen bonding
task: Elucidate hydrogen bonding as the dominant mechanism in paper fiber strength via liquid-environment perturbations
key_results: Hydrogen-bond-disrupting solvents cause pronounced strength loss; electrostatic screening and hydrophobic modifications minor effect; strong agreement with Campbell 1933 model; parallels observed between solvent strength loss and hornification
comments: Systematic solvent-based approach provides clear experimental evidence reviving the classical Campbell model over recent interpretations minimizing hydrogen bonding's role.

model_io.model: Paper wet tensile strength measurement under varied liquid environments
inputs: water, organic solvents (varying H-bond capability), salt solutions, urea solutions
outputs: correlation with liquid H-bonding disruption ability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hydrogen bonding is the dominant inter-fiber adhesion mechanism; electrostatic and hydrophobic contributions are secondary
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; H-bond disruptors cause sharp strength loss; salt/urea minor effects; conceptual link to hornification established

title: Decrease of magnetocaloric effect and magnetic susceptibility of ferromagnet due to magnetostructural phase transition
task: Quantify magnetocaloric effect reduction due to magnetostructural phase transition
key_results: Magnetic-field-induced temperature change of ~1 K at 20 kOe (below 5 K threshold for giant MCE); MSPT increases spin-exchange energy density, reducing magnetic susceptibility
comments: The work highlights that sharp magnetization changes do not guarantee large MCE, an important caveat for materials design.

model_io.model: Theoretical ferromagnetic MSPT model

hypotheses.hypothesis: MSPT increases spin-exchange energy and decreases MCE in Ni-Mn-Ga-Cu
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; temperature change ~1 K at 20 kOe, well below giant MCE threshold

title: Lead-free Cs2MH6 (M = Ge, Sn) vacancy-ordered double perovskites for optoelectronic applications: a first-principles study
task: Assess lead-free Cs₂MH₆ (M=Ge,Sn) double perovskite hydrides for optoelectronics via DFT
key_results: Direct band gaps: 1.60 eV (Cs₂GeH₆) and 1.80 eV (Cs₂SnH₆); high optical absorption in visible; thermodynamically and dynamically stable; mechanically robust with Debye temperatures elevated in Ge variant
comments: Mixed ionic-covalent bonding and visible-range absorption make these compounds promising for photovoltaics, though device performance validation is needed.

model_io.model: DFT-based structural and property prediction (Fm3̄m structure)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cs₂MH₆ vacancy-ordered double perovskites exhibit direct band gaps and strong visible absorption suitable for photovoltaics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Eg = 1.60–1.80 eV; high absorption; mechanical robustness verified by elastic analysis

title: Radiation enhanced dual-band MIMO antenna with mutual coupling reduction for 6G upper mid-band and mmWave wireless communication and sensing
task: Design compact dual-band 6G MIMO antenna with mutual coupling reduction
key_results: Dual-band operation: 7.1–13.87 GHz (S11 < −10 dB) and 24.15–27.2 GHz; mutual coupling reduced >9 dB (−16 to −25 dB); gain 4.03 dBi (mid-band) and 6.43 dBi (mmWave); element spacing 0.116λ₀
comments: The slotted parasitic decoupling element effectively reduces coupling while maintaining quasi-omnidirectional patterns despite tight spacing.

model_io.model: 2-port MIMO antenna with stub-loaded monopole, DGS, U-slot patch, and parasitic decoupler

hypotheses.hypothesis: Slotted conducting parasitic element reduces mutual coupling while maintaining omnidirectional pattern
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 9 dB reduction achieved; excellent MIMO diversity metrics maintained

title: Proof of concept of a graphene-based reconfigurable frequency multiplier fabricated within the 2D Experimental Pilot Line
task: Demonstrate reconfigurable graphene-based frequency multiplier from 2D-EPL wafer-scale fabrication
key_results: Split-gate graphene FET synthesizes W-shaped transfer characteristic enabling ×2, ×3, ×4 harmonic reconfiguration; spectral purities: 48% (doubler), 69% (tripler), 19% (quadrupler) at 100 kHz input
comments: First 2D-EPL multi-project wafer demonstration of a reconfigurable circuit; spectral purity varies significantly with multiplication order, suggesting room for optimization.

model_io.model: Split-gate graphene FET frequency multiplier

hypotheses.hypothesis: Split-gate graphene FET enables electrically reconfigurable frequency multiplication via W-shaped transfer curve
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ×2, ×3, ×4 multiplication demonstrated with varying spectral purity; no fixed tuning required
